source_consistency_checks.tolerance_rule: abs(published - recomputed) <= 100*(0.5e-d_cfd/|cfd| + 0.5e-d_exp/|exp|); the bound is derived from the printed decimals of the source columns

cross_repository_backcheck.declared_citation_verbatim: # KP505 reference data (Fujisawa et al. 2000, SIMMAN 2008)

criteria.statement: every table number carries file + sha256 + line + field + verbatim line
the artefact can be re-read against the sources and reproduces every number
the source's own error columns reproduce from its own CFD/Experimental columns
criteria.threshold: every row within the 3-decimal round-off bound (see tolerance_rule)

criteria.statement: the design advance ratio J = 0.70 is in the transcribed set
the transcribed Experimental columns equal the pinned anchor table
the KP505 constants circulating in TensorLBM are the values of the source table
every advance ratio of the circulating table is an advance ratio of the source table
criteria.threshold: 0 entries outside [0.1, 1.0] (the source table spans J = 0.1 ... 1.0)

honest_notes: The anchor is a SECONDARY_REPRODUCTION of the KRISO KP505 open-water test: the numbers come from the Experimental columns of Table 2 of Iftikhar & Takinaci (MARINE 2023), which does not cite the primary handout. Any accuracy claim built on it inherits that one tabulation step.
The cross-repository check (T6) is deliberately a *negative* finding when it fails: it is reported so that downstream papers stop quoting the circulating constants as if they were the KP505 table.

papers/data/w20-anchors/sources/lbm_bench_propeller_kp505_excerpt.txt holds the verbatim circulating block inside this repository, so the back-check can be re-run without access to the TensorLBM working tree.
